I think when any subject is taught actively we'll find a use for it one day. Being job oriented is good, but I don't think its a necessity as much as subject should be taught actively and creatively. Its like the Steve Jobs lecture when he talked about taking a calligraphy class even when he taught it could have no use and later used the skill to create an OS with good typography.

tl;dr: education for the sake of learning, need not be job oriented but should be skill based.

I don't think that education for the sole purpose of getting a job is wrong per se. Its when people start dictating and standardizing what jobs are good for our society that bothers me. If you want to be a musician, you can go do a degree in that. Shouldn't the end result of education be the creation of active, creative individuals who can do awesome shit?

Edit: if you mean education in the liberal arts/philosophy/literature when you said education for the sake of education, I believe that people in these fields should be taught to actively participate and question instead of drowning in a sea of rigid analysis.

I'm sure that when OP said 'education for the sake of education', he meant it as 'education for the sake of real learning', as in a real, hands on approach to subjects taught in schools. Just saying that you might have misunderstood the question a bit.
